text: {"final": {"findings": [{"id": "R1", "statement": "register_household(record: dict) -> Household (registry/register.py, lines 36-56) loads households, sets record['id'] via next_household_id(households) only when 'id' is missing (record.setdefault), sets 'registered' to today().isoformat() when missing, builds Household.from_dict(record), then validates: raises ValueError(f\"unknown region {household.region!r}\") if region not in region_codes(); raises ValueError(\"a household needs at least one member\") if no members; raises ValueError(f\"household {household.id} is already registered\") if the id already exists. Only after all checks pass does it append and call save_households(households). There is currently NO validation of the household ID format, so a mistyped ID like HH-10471 is accepted as long as it is not a duplicate.", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R2", "statement": "Household ID format is 'HH-NNNNC': four digits then one check digit (core/ids.py docstring). The check digit is a Mod-11 computed by household_check_digit(base: str) -> int | None, which raises ValueError(f\"household ID base must be 4 digits, got {base!r}\") if base is not exactly 4 digits, computes total = sum(int(d)*w for d,w in zip(base, CHECK_WEIGHTS)) with CHECK_WEIGHTS = (5,4,3,2), check = (11 - total % 11) % 11, and returns None when check == 10 (such bases are never issued).", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R3", "statement": "make_household_id(number: int) -> str (core/ids.py, lines 37-42) builds base = f\"{number:04d}\", gets check = household_check_digit(base), raises ValueError(f\"base {base} has no valid check digit; use the next number\") if check is None, and returns f\"HH-{base}{check}\". This is the canonical generator for valid IDs.", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R4", "statement": "There is no existing function in core/ids.py that validates an already-formed household ID string (e.g. checking that a given 'HH-NNNNC' has a correct check digit). The only validation helpers are household_check_digit (validates a 4-digit base and returns the expected check digit) and make_household_id (generates an ID from a number). A validator for a full ID string would need to be added, or the check could be done by extracting the base and comparing household_check_digit(base) to the final character.", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R5", "statement": "register_household already imports household_check_digit and make_household_id from core.ids (registry/register.py line 5: 'from core.ids import household_check_digit, make_household_id'), so the check-digit function is already available in that module for use in ID validation.", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R6", "statement": "The Household dataclass (core/models.py, lines 23-53) has fields: id: str, region: str, site: str, phone: str, members: list[Member], registered: str, status: str = 'active', sms_ok: bool = True, shelter_damaged: bool = False, income_lost: bool = False, disability: bool = False, merged_into: str | None = None. It has a from_dict classmethod used by register_household.", "file": "core/models.py"}, {"id": "R7", "statement": "The existing duplicate-ID check in register_household (line: 'if any(h.id == household.id for h in households): raise ValueError(f\"household {household.id} is already registered\")') only catches exact duplicates of already-registered IDs. A mistyped ID like HH-10471 (wrong check digit for base 1047) would pass this check and be saved as a new record, which is the bug described in the ticket.", "file": "registry/register.py"}]}}
